newsitem.title: UK: Credit Local soon to set benchmark dlr bond-Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Credit Local soon to set benchmark dlr bond-Nomura.

text.p: French bank Credit Local de France will launch a large liquid benchmark dollar deal in the coming weeks, an official at lead manager Nomura said on Wednesday.
"We expect a maturity of anywhere between five and 10 years," Nomura syndicate manager Andrew Asbury said, adding the size would be for between $500 and $1.0 billion.
"It will be a large dollar institutionally-targeted deal."
"Credit Local is looking at the market right now and will launch in the coming weeks," he said.
Syndicate officials away from the deal said at five-years a yield spread of around 20 basis points over U.S. Treasuries looked likely.
The borrower last tapped the dollar sector in November last year, a $100 million five-year offering at a yield spread of 11 b.p. over U.S. Treasuries.
It issued a $300 million five-year bond in May last year to yield 20 b.p. over U.S. Treasuries.
On Monday Standard & Poor's Corp lowered the rating on the long-term debt of Credit Local and its subsidiaries to AA+ from AAA but modified its outlook to stable from negative.
Moody's Investors Service rates Credit Local AA1.
Credit Local is held by Dexia France and Dexia Belgium since its alliance with Credit Communal de Belqique.
